definitions.explanation: A small duck of East Asia; the drake has bright orange and green plumage. Pairs are seen together, so the bird stands for a devoted couple. Written {鴛鴦|おしどり} in kanji.

examples.english: There are mandarin ducks on the pond.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧おしどり⟦{夫婦|ふうふ}→夫婦：03592_fuufu⟧だ。
examples.english: Those two are a devoted couple.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{色鮮|いろあざ}やか→色鮮やか：15312_iroazayaka⟧なオシドリ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧オス⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{池|いけ}→池：00848_ike⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{現|あらわ}れる→現れる：01870_arawareru⟧。
examples.english: In winter, brightly colored male mandarin ducks appear on the park pond.

notes:
Written in katakana as the name of the bird, and usually in hiragana in the figurative expression おしどり⟦{夫婦|ふうふ}→夫婦：03592_fuufu⟧.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- おしどり⟦{夫婦|ふうふ}→夫婦：03592_fuufu⟧: a devoted, inseparable married couple
- おしどり⟦コンビ→コンビ：27903_konbi⟧: a well-matched pair (in sports, comedy, etc.)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The image of the faithful pair comes from Chinese tradition; in reality mandarin ducks take new mates each year, a fact often cited as an irony.
